rag.description: Save extraction results straight into a SQL Server table. It validates the source and table name, creates the schema, table, and new columns on demand, accepts stored credentials or connection strings, and never changes existing columns or rows, so repeated collection runs stay reliable as pages change.

qa.question: What does the SqlServerDataCollector plugin do?
qa.answer: It writes the entities produced by an extraction rule into a SQL Server table, one row per entity and one column per content key.

qa.question: What are the key properties of SqlServerDataCollector?
qa.answer: Source (required) is a credentials name or id or a raw connection string, Repository is the table (default default-warehouse in dbo), ForEntity selects per-entity or end-of-extraction writes, and Type must be SqlServerDataCollector.

qa.question: How does SqlServerDataCollector connect to an extraction workflow?
qa.answer: An extraction rule names it in its dataCollector setting, and the extraction scope invokes it with the extracted entities as a DataCollector rule.

qa.question: What are best practices for SqlServerDataCollector?
qa.answer: Use a stored credentials record as Source, keep content keys stable because each key becomes a column, and transform the NVARCHAR(MAX) text in SQL when typed data is needed.

qa.question: How is a rule that uses SqlServerDataCollector structured?
qa.answer: Use an Extraction rule with argument {{$ --Scope:Elements}}, Content child rules for each key, and a dataCollector object with type SqlServerDataCollector, source, repository, and forEntity.

qa.question: What is the manifest key of this plugin?
What is the pluginType of SqlServerDataCollector?
What manifest version does SqlServerDataCollector use?
Which namespace, categories, and platforms apply to SqlServerDataCollector?
qa.answer: The namespace is G4.Plugins.SqlServer, the categories are DataManagement and SqlServer, and the supported platform is Any.

qa.question: Who is the author of SqlServerDataCollector?
Where are the documentation and source code for SqlServerDataCollector?
qa.answer: The description covers writing extraction results to an automatically created SQL Server table. Documentation: https://github.com/g4-api/g4-plugins/blob/main/docs/DataCollectors/SqlServerDataCollector.md. Source: https://github.com/g4-api/g4-plugins/blob/main/src/G4.Plugins.SqlServer/DataCollectors/SqlServerDataCollector.cs.

qa.question: How does SqlServerDataCollector handle errors?
qa.answer: The write fails when Source resolves no server, the login cannot create or insert, the server is older than SQL Server 2017, or a content key exceeds 128 characters; an extraction without entities writes nothing.

description: ### Purpose
SqlServerDataCollector saves the results of an extraction rule into a SQL Server table.
Each extracted entity becomes one row, and each content key becomes a column, so scraped or captured data is ready for SQL queries and reports.
It removes manual table preparation because it creates the schema, the table, and new columns on demand.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature | Description |
| Extraction integration | Receives the entities of an extraction rule through its dataCollector setting and writes them to the Repository table. |
| Automatic table creation | Creates the schema and the table when they do not exist, with one NVARCHAR(MAX) NULL column per content key. |
| Schema growth | Adds NVARCHAR(MAX) NULL columns for new content keys and never alters or drops existing columns or rows. |
| Bulk insert | Inserts all entities of a write in one bulk copy, using the union of the content keys of every entity. |
| Value storage | Stores text values as-is, missing values as NULL, and numbers, booleans, objects, and arrays as minified JSON text. |
| Flexible connection | Resolves Source as a stored credentials record by name or id, or as a raw connection string. |
| Write modes | Writes each entity as soon as it is extracted (ForEntity true) or all entities once at the end (ForEntity false). |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case | Description |
| Web scraping to SQL Server | Stores listings, prices, or contacts scraped from pages directly in a database table. |
| Lead and record capture | Collects leads or records from web portals into a shared sales or operations table. |
| Central data store | Gives other services and reports one SQL Server table to query instead of local files. |
| Incremental collection | Appends new rows on every run and grows the table when pages start showing new fields. |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case | Description |
| UI data snapshots | Saves values read from the application under test so later SQL queries can compare them with expected data. |
| Cross-run comparison | Keeps extraction results from several runs in one table to spot changes between builds. |
### Requirements and Limitations
| Item | Description |
| SQL Server version | Requires SQL Server 2017 or later, or Azure SQL, because table preparation uses STRING_AGG and OPENJSON. |
| Permissions | The login needs rights to create schemas, create and alter tables, and insert rows when those objects are missing. |
| Text columns | Every column the collector creates is NVARCHAR(MAX) NULL; convert values in SQL when typed columns are needed. |
| Column names | A content key longer than 128 characters is rejected, because SQL Server cannot name such a column. |
| Empty extraction | An extraction without entities writes nothing and does not open a connection. |

annotations.expected_result: Every lead row on the page is inserted into sales.Leads with Name, Email, and Company columns in one bulk insert after the extraction finishes.
annotations.notes: The stored credentials record sql-production supplies the connection. The schema sales, the table Leads, and missing columns are created as NVARCHAR(MAX) NULL when needed.

description: ### Collect extracted leads into a SQL Server table
The extraction rule reads the name, email, and company from each lead row matched by the XPath `//table[@id='leads']//tr[td]`.

The `dataCollector` setting sends the entities to `SqlServerDataCollector`, which writes them to `sales.Leads` through the stored credentials record `sql-production` once the extraction finishes (`forEntity` is `false`).

annotations.expected_result: Each product card is inserted as its own row into dbo.[default-warehouse] as soon as it is extracted.
annotations.notes: Without a repository, the collector writes to the table default-warehouse in the dbo schema. A raw connection string is used because the value contains an equals sign.

description: ### Stream extracted entities into the default table
The extraction rule reads the title and price of each product card matched by the XPath `//div[@class='product']`.
With `forEntity` set to `true` and no `repository`, every entity is written right away to the `default-warehouse` table in `dbo` through a raw connection string.
Set to true to write each extracted entity to the table as soon as it is extracted.
Set to false to write all extracted entities together after the extraction finishes, in one bulk insert.
Writing per entity keeps rows flowing during long extractions, while writing at the end needs fewer round trips.
properties.name: ForEntity

description: Names the destination table, as table, schema.table, or a bracketed name such as [sales].[Leads].
A name without a schema uses the dbo schema, and an empty value uses the table default-warehouse.
The schema and the table are created automatically when they do not exist.
properties.name: Repository

description: Names a stored SQL Server credentials record by its name or id, so the login stays out of the automation definition.
When no record matches, a value that contains an equals sign is used as a raw ADO.NET connection string.
Any other unmatched value is used as a raw Microsoft Entra access token, which has no server of its own and is therefore rejected.
properties.name: Source

description: Enter SqlServerDataCollector so the extracted data is written to SQL Server by this collector.
A different value sends the data to another collector, such as a file or SQLite collector.
properties.name: Type

summary: Writes extracted data into a SQL Server table, one row per extracted entity, using fast bulk insert.
Creates the schema, the table, and any missing columns automatically, so extraction results land in the database without setup.
Connects through a stored credentials record or a connection string and never changes existing columns or rows.
